later_classification: Aquaporin-4-IgG neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder vs MS
scientific_basis: AQP4-IgG, distinct immunopathogenesis, clinical/radiological phenotype, prognosis and treatment response established NMOSD as distinct from MS.
Reproducible live cell-based MOG-IgG assays plus distinct phenotype, course and treatment outcomes support separation from MS and AQP4-NMOSD, while criteria remain under continuing validation.
Single-gene causes produce reproducible beta-cell defects, familial patterns and gene-specific treatment implications; genetic diagnosis can reverse T1/T2 misclassification.

unified_entity: Childhood sarcoma/lymphoma and non-Hodgkin lymphoma categories
scientific_basis: Distinctive epidemiology, morphology, germinal-center phenotype, MYC rearrangement and EBV associations established a reproducible lymphoma entity with distinctive treatment needs.

later_classification: Endemic/sporadic/immunodeficiency-associated subtypes later challenged by EBV-positive vs EBV-negative biology
scientific_basis: Geographic/clinical epidemiologic categories were useful historically but molecular data show EBV status better captures biological heterogeneity across geography and immune status.
Clinical and histological manifestations track host cell-mediated immunity along an ordered spectrum; high clinicopathological concordance supports a continuum rather than separate diseases.
Serotypes differ in autoimmunity, genetics and some prognosis, but seronegative RA remains heterogeneous and evidence is insufficient to treat the two as clean separate diseases.

later_classification: Sepsis/severe sepsis/septic shock revised to Sepsis-3 sepsis plus septic-shock subset
scientific_basis: SIRS-based continuum had inadequate specificity and sensitivity; severe sepsis was judged redundant and definitions were rebuilt around organ dysfunction and higher-risk shock.
EF categories predict some treatment differences and standardize care, but LVEF is continuous, cut-points are partly arbitrary and HFpEF is mechanistically heterogeneous.
Initial morphology correlated with molecular differences, but type 2 proved molecularly heterogeneous and WHO 2022 eliminated the type 1/2 binary subcategorization.
Type 1 has strong orexin/hypocretin biological coherence; type 2 lacks an equivalent positive biomarker and shows materially lower diagnostic stability on repeated MSLT testing.

later_classification: EGFR-, ALK-, ROS1-, KRAS- and other driver-defined subgroups
scientific_basis: Actionable genomic alterations define reproducible tumor biology and produce large mechanism-aligned treatment differences with targeted inhibitors.

later_classification: Sporadic, genetic and acquired prion diseases with molecular/pathological subtypes
scientific_basis: Distinct sporadic, PRNP-genetic and acquired etiologies coexist with reproducible clinicopathological and prion-protein subtypes.

later_classification: Schizophrenia vs bipolar/affective psychosis Kraepelinian dichotomy
scientific_basis: Clinical utility of the dichotomy persists, but genetics, neurophysiology, symptoms and treatment response overlap substantially and challenge a strict binary disease boundary.
Reproducible morphology, different precursor pathways, KRAS/BRAF/ERBB2 vs TP53-dominant molecular profiles, course and chemotherapy sensitivity support biological separation.

later_classification: GPA/MPA/EGPA clinical entities versus PR3-ANCA/MPO-ANCA cross-cutting biology
scientific_basis: Genetic, prognostic and treatment-relevant differences often align more strongly with PR3/MPO specificity than traditional clinicopathologic labels, showing that accepted categories can be cross-cut by stronger biology.
The categories represent an imaging-defined continuum/stage framework; some patients progress while many do not, so absence of transition does not imply separate diseases.
Subtypes help communication and treatment selection but symptom/stool patterns can change over time and do not establish distinct biological diseases.

unified_entity: Diabetes in lean undernourished young people
scientific_basis: Described since 1955, classified by WHO in 1985, removed in 1999, and re-recognized by IDF in 2025; newer metabolic studies suggest impaired insulin secretion without typical T1 autoimmunity or T2 insulin resistance, but diagnostic and causal uncertainties remain.
